content: 1. Prolonged use of CYP3A4 inhibitors for more than one month is not recommended. Medications such as elagolix and cobicistat, which affect hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism, require careful monitoring and potential therapy adjustments. 2. The combination of elagolix (a weak-to-moderate CYP3A4 inducer) with cobicistat (a CYP3A4 inhibitor and substrate) may lead to increased elagolix levels and decreased cobicistat levels. Refer to the prescribing information for both drugs to determine appropriate dosage adjustments. 3. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 4. Cobicistat inhibits P-glycoprotein (P-gp), and encorafenib may increase the levels or effects of tenofovir AF through other mechanisms. Therapy adjustments and close monitoring are advised. 5. Encorafenib, a BCRP inhibitor, can elevate the concentration and toxicity of BCRP substrates. Monitor for signs of increased exposure and consider dose adjustments for these substrates. 6. Encorafenib affects CYP3A4 metabolism by both inhibiting and inducing it at clinically relevant plasma concentrations. Co-administration with sensitive CYP3A4 substrates may increase toxicity or reduce efficacy. Use caution and monitor closely. 7. Cobicistat increases the toxicity of enfortumab vedotin by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Enfortumab vedotin, an antibody-drug conjugate, releases monomethyl auristatin E (MMAE) via proteolytic cleavage, and MMAE is primarily metabolized by CYP3A4. Monitor for toxicities and adjust therapy as needed. 8. Co-administration of dual P-gp and strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase MMAE exposure, raising the risk of enfortumab vedotin toxicities. Monitor closely for signs of toxicity. 9. Enzalutamide decreases cobicistat levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 10. Elvitegravir reduces the levels or effects of erdafitinib by affecting CYP2C9/10 metabolism. If co-administration is necessary, start with an 8-mg/day dose of erdafitinib, with potential increases based on serum phosphate levels and tolerability. 11. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of erlotinib by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. If co-administration is unavoidable, reduce the erlotinib dose in 50 mg increments and monitor for adverse effects. 12. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of escitalopram by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 13. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of esomeprazole by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 14. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of estradiol vaginal formulations by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with CYP3A4 inhibitors may elevate plasma concentrations of estrogens and their associated toxicities. 15. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of ethosuximide by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 16. Fedratinib increases cobicistat levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust the dose of CYP3A4 substrates as necessary. 17. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of felodipine by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 18. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of fentanyl by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. If co-administration is necessary, monitor for respiratory depression and sedation at frequent intervals and adjust the fentanyl dose until stable effects are achieved. 19. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of fentanyl intranasal formulations by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor for respiratory depression and sedation, and adjust the fentanyl dose as needed. 20. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of flecainide by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Clinical monitoring is recommended when co-administered with antiarrhythmics. 21. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of fluoxetine. Carefully titrate the antidepressant dose to achieve the desired effect, using the lowest feasible initial or maintenance dose, and monitor its response during co-administration with SSRIs and cobicistat. 22. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of flurazepam by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 23. Cobicistat increases the levels of fluticasone furoate and inhaled fluticasone by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 24. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of fluvastatin by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. For HMG-CoA reductase inhibitors not contraindicated with cobicistat, start with the lowest recommended dose and titrate while monitoring for safety. 25. Fluvoxamine increases cobicistat levels or effects. Carefully titrate the antidepressant dose to the desired effect, using the lowest feasible initial or maintenance dose, and monitor its response during co-administration with SSRIs and cobicistat. 26. Elvitegravir, a CYP3A4 substrate, may have increased levels when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Use caution and monitor closely. 27. Isoniazid increases cobicistat and elvitegravir levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 28. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of isradipine by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 29. Istradefylline increases elvitegravir levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 30. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of itraconazole by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy adjustments and close monitoring are required. 31. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of ivacaftor by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Reduce the ivacaftor dose if co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 32. Ketoconazole increases elvitegravir levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. If co-administered, limit the ketoconazole dose to 200 mg/day; no dose adjustment is needed for elvitegravir. 33. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of lansoprazole by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 34. Lenacapavir increases elvitegravir and cobicistat levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 35. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of lettermovir by decreasing its metabolism. Co-administration with OATP1B1/3 inhibitors may elevate lettermovir plasma concentrations. 36. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of levamlodipine by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with moderate and strong CYP3A inhibitors may require dose reduction of amlodipine. Monitor for symptoms of hypotension and edema. 37. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of levoketoconazole by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy adjustments and close monitoring are required.
